Subject: Subprocessor notice — DataStream Solutions (logging)

Hi Rafael,

Per our MSA (section 5.4), Acme is notifying Redwood of a planned subprocessor engagement: DataStream Solutions Ltd. (UK entity). They will provide centralized logging and ephemeral metric aggregation for the new connector we discussed.

Quick details attached (Acme_Subprocessor_List_20261125.pdf) — scope, proposed access, and a draft DPA between Acme and DataStream. High-level:
- Purpose: log ingestion & retention for performance troubleshooting and alerting
- Data types: application-level logs and non-identifying metadata (no customer PII projected)
- Retention: 30 days (default), can be shortened by request

Can you confirm whether Redwood requires any additional flow-down language in the DPA (e.g., breach notification times, right to audit, geographic restrictions) or additional evidence (SOC reports) before we proceed? Procurement expects sign-off within three business days to meet the integration schedule.

If you prefer, we can share the DataStream SOC2 snapshot and the signed DPAs once countersigned.

Thanks and happy to hop on a 15-min call if that's easier.

Best,

Rafael / Elena — reviewed the materials you sent. Please see high-level legal intake below and attached redline document (Redline_Subprocessor_Clauses_20261128.docx). Key asks: 

- Flow-down: Redwood requires that any subprocessor contract with DataStream contain flow-down obligations matching the Redwood-Acme DPA: data processing purposes, security measures, deletion/return obligations, and identical breach notification timelines (48 hours initial notice, 7 days substantive update).
- Right to audit: If DataStream will host logs that could contain customer-identifying metadata, we need either (a) a contractual right to audit (on-site or SOC2) or (b) an attestation to a current SOC2 Type II with applicable trust services criteria.
- Sub-subcontracting: DataStream should not engage further subprocessors without Acme obtaining prior written consent from Redwood (or Acme must ensure equivalent flow-down).
- Cross-border: If DataStream processes data outside the EU, include standard transfer mechanisms (SCCs) or confirm processing stays in UK/EU.
- Retention: 30 days is acceptable but require the DPA to include a retention cap and a mechanism for us to request earlier deletion.

Evidence requested before procurement approval: current SOC2 report (redacted OK), network diagram showing access controls, and the signed DataStream DPA (or a redline of the draft).

Procurement note: any deviation from the flow-down language will need an escalation to VP Prod or legal leadership.

If Acme prefers, Redwood can provide a short template clause set for insertion. I attached our suggested redlines and a short comment summary.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Laura / Rafael — thanks for the detailed notes. Quick responses and attached evidence: DataStream_Scope.pdf and DataProcessing_Addendum_DataStream.pdf (draft signed by Acme).

- PII: Confirmed — DataStream will not receive direct customer PII. They will receive hashed request identifiers and application logs (no cleartext user identifiers). We can contractually limit fields if Redwood wants.
- SOC2: DataStream has a current SOC2 Type II report covering logging/service operations; snapshot attached.
- Processing locations: primary UK data centers, secondary EU region (Frankfurt). No US processing planned for this engagement.
- Retention: default 30 days; we can offer a 14-day variant for EU customers if needed.
- DPA: Acme has executed a DPA with DataStream; attaching the countersigned addendum. We are happy to accept Redwood's redlines or to receive a template clause from you for insertion.

Requested timeline: Procurement needs final sign-off by end-of-week Nov 30 to keep the integration schedule. Happy to get onto a call this afternoon if that helps.

Elena

1) We receive the SOC2 Type II evidence (redacted OK) and a confirmation that the scope includes logging operations (we have the snapshot but need verification that current date covers the control period).

If both items are met, I authorize Rafael to sign the subprocessor delegation notice (we'll use the Delegation_notice_template_20261130.pdf) and update the order form accordingly. If any of the above is missing or materially different, we will escalate to the Legal Ops director for an exception.
